items.title: Silver by Fire, Silver by Mercury: A Chemical History of Silver Refining in New Spain and Mexico, 16th to 19th Centuries
items.note: Reconstructs refining chemistry and mercury consumption in New Spain and offers production estimates by treasury district, a check on registered output series.

items.title: Global Quantification and Inventory Demand for Silver in China
items.who: J. Cao and D. O. Flynn
items.note: Uses Qing wealth-confiscation records for a partial estimate of silver held in China around 1750, proposing stocks as a check on legal and contraband import flows.

items.title: The Changing Significance of Latin American Silver in the Chinese Economy, 16th–19th Centuries
items.note: Updated synthesis of import estimates and of silver's changing monetary role in China across three centuries.

items.title: Creating Global Demand: Polycentric Approaches, Crossroads of Silk and Silver in China and Iberian Empires during the Early Modern Era
items.note: Introduces a themed issue on silver accumulation by Chinese merchants and demand for goods across the Manila and Macao routes.

items.title: Global circulation of silver between Ming–Qing China and the Americas: Combining historical texts and scientific analyses
items.who: L. Sun, G. Yang, R. Liu, A. M. Pollard et al.
items.note: Pilot compositional study finding Ming and Qing bullion purer than American coins, and proposing chemical analysis as an independent source on silver flows.

items.title: Empire of Silver: A New Monetary History of China
items.note: English translation of a Chinese monetary history that treats Ming silverization and foreign silver within a long-run account of the currency system.

items.title: The economics of the Manila Galleon
items.venue: Journal of Chinese Economic and Foreign Trade Studies
items.note: Reviews the quantitative and qualitative evidence on the galleon trade for economists and frames its impact in a world-systems model.

items.title: The Cambridge Economic History of China, vol. 1: To 1800
items.who: D. Ma and R. von Glahn (eds.)
items.note: Reference volume with chapters on Ming and Qing money, trade and fiscal systems, synthesizing current views of imported silver to 1800.

items.title: Overlooked Silver: Reassessing Ming–Qing Silver Supplies
items.note: Estimates from slag dumps at southwestern mines an output of 20,000–50,000 tons of silver, a domestic supply that would reduce the share of imports.

items.title: Spending a Windfall: American Precious Metals and Euro-Asian Trade
items.who: N. Palma and A. C. Silva
items.note: Quantified how American bullion financed European imports from Asia, a key link in the Cape-route component of flows to China.

items.title: Current Debates about the Colonial Economy and Government from the Spanish Royal Treasury Records
items.note: Surveys what the TePaske–Klein treasury accounts can and cannot show, including inter-treasury transfers relevant to Acapulco remittances.

items.title: Seeing is believing: The colour of silver alloys and the global silver circulation in the Chinese Ming and Qing dynasties
items.who: L. Sun, G. Yang, R. Guo et al.
items.note: Models how copper and lead content affected the visible colour of silver, linking assaying by eye to the circulation of foreign and domestic silver.

items.title: The Manila correspondencia and the institutional underpinnings of the trans-Pacific silver trade in the long eighteenth century
items.who: J. J. Rivas Moreno and G. Ruiz-Stovel
items.note: Builds a database of all extant respondentia contracts in Manila notarial records, 1736–1800, tracing how the silver trade was financed.
